title: CentripetalNet: Pursuing High-quality Keypoint Pairs for Object Detection

problem.summary: In corner/keypoint-based detectors the hard step is pairing the two keypoints of the same object: associative-embedding matching is trained with push/pull losses that become unstable with multiple similar objects, and it uses only appearance so similar-looking objects far apart get confused. Anchor-based detectors meanwhile require hand-designed anchors and suffer positive/negative imbalance.
statements: Corner-based detectors still produce incorrect keypoint pairs, which directly degrades detection performance.
Associative embedding matching is highly sensitive to outliers and training becomes much harder when several similar objects appear in one image.
Embedding prediction ignores position information, so two similar-appearance objects far apart receive similar embeddings.
Anchor-based detectors make anchors hard to hand-design and suffer an imbalance between negative and positive anchor boxes.

evidence.quote: However, incorrect keypoint matching is still widespread and greatly affects the performance of the detector.
it is difficult to manually design a set of suitable anchors
It is highly sensitive to outliers and the training difficulty will increase dramatically when there are multiple similar objects in one training sample.
the embedding prediction is based on the appearance feature without using position information

background.summary: The paper builds on the corner-based line started by CornerNet (boxes as keypoint pairs grouped by associative embedding) and CenterNet (adds a center heatmap as validation), plus the anchor-free alternatives FCOS/ExtremeNet/RepPoints and the anchor-based two-stage and one-stage baselines. The claimed gap is the grouping/matching step, not corner prediction.

relatedWork.name: CornerNet
relatedWork.relation: prior method that represents a box as a top-left/bottom-right corner pair grouped by associative embedding; the framework the paper extends
relatedWork.quote: the CornerNet [17] proposes a novel method to represent a bounding box as a pair of corners, i.e, top-left corner and bottom-right corner.

relatedWork.name: CenterNet
relatedWork.relation: adds a center detection branch to CornerNet and validates corners by center prediction, but cannot handle dense cases
relatedWork.quote: CenterNet [7] adds a center detection branch into CornerNet and largely improves the performance by center point validation.

relatedWork.name: FCOS
relatedWork.relation: anchor-free center/point-based baseline treating all points inside a box as positives
relatedWork.quote: FCOS [31] treats all the points inside the bounding box of the object as positive samples.

relatedWork.name: RetinaNet
relatedWork.relation: anchor-based baseline that addresses classification imbalance with focal loss
relatedWork.quote: RetinaNet [20] uses focal loss to mitigate classification imbalance problem.

relatedWork.name: Mask R-CNN
relatedWork.relation: two-stage instance segmentation prior; its RoIAlign layer is reused in the proposed mask head
relatedWork.quote: Mask R-CNN [11] replaces the RoIPool layer with the RoIAlign layer using bilinear interpolation.

evidence.quote: The corner-based detection framework can be divided into two steps including corner points prediction and corner matching.
These methods usually achieve high recall with quite many false detections.

solution.summary: CentripetalNet pairs corners by predicting for each corner a centripetal shift (a log-scaled 2-D offset to the box center) and matching corners whose decoded centers coincide inside a central region, re-scoring pairs by center proximity. A cross-star deformable convolution, guided by the corner-to-center shift, adapts corner-pooling features, and a RoIAlign mask head adds instance segmentation.
solution.approach: Match top-left and bottom-right corners by requiring their predicted centripetal shifts to decode to the same box center, and adapt corner features with a cross-star deformable convolution whose offset field encodes the guiding shift.
components: centripetal shift module predicting log-scaled corner-to-center offsets and a central-region matching rule with score re-weighting
cross-star deformable convolution whose offset field is supervised by the guiding shift (corner to center)
corner prediction inherited from the CornerNet pipeline (corner heatmaps + local offsets, Hourglass backbone)
instance mask head using RoIAlign on predicted boxes, four 3x3 conv layers and a transposed conv to a 28 x 28 mask
multi-task training loss combining detection, offset, guiding shift, centripetal shift and mask terms
soft-NMS at test time to select final boxes

evidence.quote: we propose CentripetalNet which uses centripetal shift to pair corner keypoints from the same instance
we design a cross-star deformable convolution network to conduct feature adaption
CentripetalNet consists of four modules, namely corner prediction module, centripetal shift module, cross-star deformable convolution, and instance mask head.
if the positions of the shifted corners are close enough, they form a bounding box with a high score.

experiments.summary: Evaluation is on MS-COCO 2017 (train2017, val2017, test-dev2017) against two-stage, anchor-based one-stage and anchor-free detectors for both detection and instance segmentation, plus ablations isolating centripetal shift, feature adaption variants and the mask branch (Hourglass-52 ablations, Hourglass-104 headline model).

benchmarks.split: ablation, Hourglass-52, centripetal shift vs 37.3 for associative embedding
ablation, Hourglass-52, cross-star deformable conv vs 40.7 with no adaption

evidence.quote: CentripetalNet with Hourglass-104 as the backbone network achieves an AP of 46.1% at single-scale and 48.0% at multi-scale on MSCOCO test-dev 2017, which are the best performance in all anchor-free detectors.
our best model achieves 38.8% AP in single-scale test, while Mask R-CNN with ResNeXt-101FPN achieves 37.5% AP.
our model achieves comparable performance with a MaskAP of 40.2%.

limitations.summary: The paper has no dedicated limitations section, but it reports that the log transform of the centripetal shift can fail under heatmap rounding, that the guiding-shift loss weight is sensitive, and the headline numbers depend on flip and multi-scale testing; no inference speed is reported.
items: The logarithm in the centripetal shift cannot always be applied because rounded heatmap offsets can be negative during training.
Performance degrades if the guiding-shift loss weight alpha is set too large.
Reported AP relies on flip augmentation and single-scale vs multi-scale test protocols; no FPS/runtime figure is given for the detector.
Evaluation is restricted to MS-COCO with Hourglass backbones, and the mask branch only uses features from the last backbone layer.

evidence.quote: during implementation, it is sometimes impossible to apply the logarithm to the offset between the ground truth corners on heatmap and precise center locations
We set α to 0.05, as we find that large α degrades the performance of the network.
We use flip augmentation by default, and report both of single-scale and multi-scale test results on MS-COCO test-dev2017.

equations.name: centripetal shift
equations.expr: cs_tl = (log((ctx - tlx)/s), log((cty - tly)/s)); cs_br = (log((brx - ctx)/s), log((bry - cty)/s))

equations.name: central region
equations.expr: Rcentral = {(x, y) | x in [ctlx, cbrx], y in [ctly, cbry]}

equations.name: pair score weight
equations.expr: wj = exp(-|brctx - tlctx| * |brcty - tlcty| / ((cbrx - ctlx) * (cbry - ctly)))

equations.name: multi-task objective
equations.expr: L = Ldet + Loff + alpha * Ldelta + Lcs + Lmask

applications.domain: autonomous driving, mobile entertainment, video surveillance
applications.detail: The introduction positions general object detection as a foundation technology for automatic driving, mobile entertainment and video surveillance applications.
applications.quote: Object detection is a fundamental topic in various applications of computer vision, such as automatic driving, mobile entertainment, and video surveillance.
